subject: maths
title: Measuring Angles
seo_title: Year 5 Measuring Angles Worksheets: Protractor, Estimating and Angle Names
standard_text: Estimate, construct and measure angles in degrees, using appropriate tools including a protractor, and relate these measures to angle names
meta_desc: Free Year 5 measuring angles worksheets for the Australian Curriculum: name acute, right, obtuse, straight and reflex angles and a revolution, estimate angles, read both protractor scales, construct angles and find angles in everyday life. 100 maths questions with an answer key, great for NAPLAN practice.
key_big: Right angle 90°, straight angle 180°, revolution 360°. Measure with a protractor and read the scale that starts at 0 on your arm.
key_sub: Estimate first: acute is less than 90°, obtuse is between 90° and 180°, reflex is between 180° and 360°. If the reading does not match your estimate, you read the wrong scale (40° and 140° sit at the same place).
body_html:
Angle names

An angle is an amount of turn between two arms. We measure it in degrees (°). A revolution (one whole turn) is 360°, a straight angle (half a turn) is 180° and a right angle (a quarter turn) is 90°.

NameSize
Acute angleless than 90°
Right angleexactly 90°
Obtuse anglemore than 90°, less than 180°
Straight angleexactly 180°
Reflex anglemore than 180°, less than 360°
Revolutionexactly 360°

Estimate first

Compare the angle with a right angle (90°) and a straight angle (180°). Is it smaller, between them or bigger? The length of the arms does not change the size of the angle.

Estimate

An angle is a bit wider than a right angle. About how big is it?

It is more than 90° but much less than 180°, so it is obtuse.

Answer: about 110° to 120°

Measure with a protractor

1. Put the centre of the protractor on the vertex. 2. Line up one arm with 0. 3. Read the scale that starts at 0 on that arm. 4. Check with your estimate: acute or obtuse?

Reflex angle

The gap on the other side of a reflex angle measures 130°. Find the reflex angle.

The two angles make a revolution: 360° − 130° = 230°.

Answer: 230°

Construct an angle

To construct 65°: draw one arm with a ruler. Put the centre of the protractor on its end and line the arm up with 0. Mark a dot at 65 on the scale that starts at that 0. Join the dot to the vertex with a ruler.

Construct a reflex angle

Construct an angle of 250°.

A protractor only goes to 180°. 360° − 250° = 110°. Construct 110°, then mark the angle round the outside.

Answer: the outside of a 110° angle

Angles around us

ExampleAngleName
Clock hands at 3 o’clock90°right angle
Clock hands at 6 o’clock180°straight angle
A house roof pitchoften 15° to 30°acute angle
A skateboarder’s “180”180°straight angle (half a turn)
A skateboarder’s “360”360°revolution (a whole turn)

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Reading the wrong scale (140° for a 40° angle)Read the scale that starts at 0 on your arm, then check your estimate
Calling 190° obtuseObtuse is between 90° and 180°. More than 180° is reflex
Saying a revolution is 180°A straight angle is 180° (half a turn). A revolution is 360° (a whole turn)
Thinking longer arms make a bigger angleThe size of an angle is the amount of turn, not the length of the arms

faq.q: What do Year 5 students learn about angles in the Australian Curriculum?
faq.a: They estimate, construct and measure angles in degrees with a protractor, and connect the sizes to the angle names: acute, right, obtuse, straight, reflex and revolution.

faq.q: How do you measure an angle with a protractor?
faq.a: Estimate first. Put the centre on the vertex, line up one arm with 0 and read the scale that starts at that 0, then check the reading against your estimate.

faq.q: What are the angle names and their sizes?
faq.a: Acute is less than 90°, right is 90°, obtuse is between 90° and 180°, straight is 180°, reflex is between 180° and 360°, and a revolution is 360°.

faq.q: Why do protractors have two scales?
faq.a: So you can measure from an arm on either side: one scale starts at 0 on the right and the other at 0 on the left. Always read the scale that starts at 0 on your arm.

items.e: A reflex angle is bigger than a straight angle but smaller than a revolution: between 180° and 360°. Look at the arc: it goes round the outside. This angle is 200°. (The gap between the arms is 160°, but the arc marks the big angle round the outside.)

items.q: An angle measures 185°. What is its name?
items.e: 185° is more than 180° but less than 360°, so it is reflex, even though it is close to a straight angle.

items.q: Liam says an angle of 190° is obtuse because it is bigger than 90°. Is he right?
items.e: Obtuse angles are bigger than 90° but smaller than 180°. 190° is more than 180°, so it is reflex.
A revolution is one whole turn: exactly 360°. The arm turns all the way round and ends where it started.

items.q: An angle measures 270°. What is its name?
items.e: 270° is more than 180° but less than 360°, so it is reflex. It is three right angles: 3 × 90° = 270°.

items.q: What is the name of the marked angle?
items.e: An acute angle is smaller than a right angle: less than 90°. This angle is 70°.

items.q: Which list goes from the smallest angle to the largest?
c: right, acute, obtuse, straight, revolution, reflex
acute, right, obtuse, reflex, straight, revolution
acute, obtuse, right, straight, reflex, revolution
acute, right, obtuse, straight, reflex, revolution
items.e: Acute is less than 90°, right is 90°, obtuse is between 90° and 180°, straight is 180°, reflex is between 180° and 360°, and a revolution is 360°.

items.q: An angle measures 360°. What is its name?
items.e: 360° is one whole turn: a revolution. A straight angle is only half a turn (180°).

items.q: An angle measures 175°. What is its name?
items.e: 175° is more than 90° but less than 180°, so it is obtuse. It is close to a straight angle, but not 180°.

items.q: How many degrees are in a revolution?
items.e: A revolution is one whole turn: 360°. It is 4 right angles: 4 × 90° = 360°. 180° is a straight angle, only half a turn.

items.q: What is the name of the marked angle?
items.e: An acute angle is smaller than a right angle: less than 90°. This angle is 35°.
A straight angle is exactly 180°, half a turn. The two arms make a straight line.

A reflex angle is bigger than a straight angle but smaller than a revolution: between 180° and 360°. Look at the arc: it goes round the outside. This angle is 230°. (The gap between the arms is 130°, but the arc marks the big angle round the outside.)
A straight angle is exactly 180°, half a turn. The two arms make a straight line. Turning the angle does not change its size or its name.
An obtuse angle is bigger than a right angle but smaller than a straight angle: between 90° and 180°. This angle is 125°.

A reflex angle is bigger than a straight angle but smaller than a revolution: between 180° and 360°. Look at the arc: it goes round the outside. This angle is 320°. (The gap between the arms is 40°, but the arc marks the big angle round the outside.)
An obtuse angle is bigger than a right angle but smaller than a straight angle: between 90° and 180°. This angle is 100°.

items.q: An angle measures 89°. What is its name?
items.e: 89° is less than 90°, so it is acute (only just). A right angle is exactly 90°.
An obtuse angle is bigger than a right angle but smaller than a straight angle: between 90° and 180°. This angle is 160°.

items.q: What is the name of the marked angle?
items.e: A right angle is exactly 90°, a quarter turn. The small square shows it. Turning the angle does not change its size or its name.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for the marked angle?
items.e: The angle is smaller than a right angle (90°), so it is acute. About 45° fits. (It is 43°.) About 135° would be a much wider angle.
The arc goes round the outside, so the angle is reflex: more than 180°. The gap on the other side is about 60°, so the marked angle is about 360° − 60° = 300°. (It is 300°.)

items.q: Which angle is closest to 45°?
items.e: 45° is half a right angle. B is about half of a right angle. A is nearly a right angle, C is very small and D is obtuse.
The angle is bigger than a right angle (90°) but smaller than a straight angle (180°), so it is obtuse. About 120° fits. (It is 118°.) About 60° would be a much smaller angle.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for the marked angle?
items.e: The angle is smaller than a right angle (90°), so it is acute. About 30° fits. (It is 28°.) About 150° would be a much wider angle.
The arc goes round the outside, so the angle is reflex: more than 180°. The gap on the other side is about 120°, so the marked angle is about 360° − 120° = 240°. (It is 235°.)

items.q: An angle is a little bigger than a straight angle. Which could it be?
items.e: A straight angle is 180°, so a little bigger is about 195°. 165° is a little smaller than a straight angle, and 95° is a little bigger than a right angle.
A reflex angle is more than 180°. Only the arc in D goes round more than a straight angle. A is obtuse: nearly 180°, but not more.
The angle is bigger than a right angle (90°) but smaller than a straight angle (180°), so it is obtuse. About 150° fits. (It is 147°.) About 30° would be a much smaller angle.
The size of an angle is the amount of turn, not the length of the arms. A is reflex (about 250°), so it is the largest, even though its arms are the shortest.
Obtuse means between 90° and 180°. D is about 145°. B is reflex: the gap between its arms looks obtuse, but the arc marks the angle round the outside.
The angle is bigger than a right angle (90°) but smaller than a straight angle (180°), so it is obtuse. About 170° fits. (It is 172°.) About 10° would be a much smaller angle.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for the marked angle?
items.e: The angle is smaller than a right angle (90°), so it is acute. About 60° fits. (It is 62°.) About 120° would be a much wider angle.
C is a bit more than a right angle: about 120°. A is about 60°. B is reflex (about 240°): its gap looks like 120°, but the arc marks the big angle. D is nearly a straight angle.

items.q: Mia estimates a reflex angle as about 70°. Why must she be wrong?
c: A reflex angle is more than 180°
A reflex angle is less than 90°
70° is too big for any angle
items.e: Every reflex angle is more than 180°, so its estimate must be more than 180°. 70° may be the gap on the other side: then the reflex angle is about 360° − 70° = 290°.
The arc goes round the outside, so the angle is reflex: more than 180°. The gap on the other side is about 160°, so the marked angle is about 360° − 160° = 200°. (It is 205°.)
The arc goes round the outside, so the angle is reflex: more than 180°. The gap on the other side is about 90°, so the marked angle is about 360° − 90° = 270°. (It is 275°.)

items.q: An angle is about half a right angle. Which is the best estimate?
items.e: A right angle is 90°, and half of 90° is 45°.

items.q: Which is larger: three right angles or 250°?
items.e: Three right angles are 3 × 90° = 270°, and 270° is more than 250°.

items.q: An angle is a little smaller than a right angle. Which could it be?
items.e: A right angle is 90°. A little smaller than 90° is about 80°. 100° is a little bigger.

items.q: Cooper measures an angle and writes 40°. The angle is clearly obtuse. What should he have written?
items.e: An obtuse angle is more than 90°. Cooper read the wrong scale: the other scale gives 180° − 40° = 140°.

items.q: What is the size of the angle?
items.e: The bottom arm is on 0 on the right, so read the inner scale, which starts at 0 on the right. The other arm crosses it at 40. The outer scale says 140 there, but it starts from the other side. The angle is smaller than a right angle, so 40° makes sense.

items.q: Neither arm is on 0. What is the size of the angle?
items.e: On the inner scale one arm is at 20 and the other is at 95. The angle is the difference: 95° − 20° = 75°.

items.q: What is the size of the angle?
items.e: The bottom arm is on 0 on the left, so read the outer scale, which starts at 0 on the left. The other arm crosses it at 145. The small marks go up in 5s, so the mark between 140 and 150 is 145. (The inner scale says 35 there.) The angle is bigger than a right angle, so 145° makes sense.

items.q: Ethan measures an angle that is clearly smaller than a right angle. The arm crosses the protractor at 35 and 145. What is the angle?
items.e: An angle smaller than a right angle is acute, less than 90°, so it is 35°. 145 is on the other scale.

items.q: What is the size of the angle?
items.e: The bottom arm is on 0 on the right, so read the inner scale, which starts at 0 on the right. The other arm crosses it at 80. The outer scale says 100 there, but it starts from the other side. The angle is smaller than a right angle, so 80° makes sense.

items.q: Where do you put the centre of the protractor when you measure an angle?
c: at the end of an arm
in the middle of an arm
items.e: The centre goes on the vertex, where the two arms meet. Then line up one arm with 0.

items.q: What is the size of the angle?
items.e: The bottom arm is on 0 on the right, so read the inner scale, which starts at 0 on the right. The other arm crosses it at 135. The small marks go up in 5s, so the mark between 130 and 140 is 135. The outer scale says 45 there, but it starts from the other side. The angle is bigger than a right angle, so 135° makes sense.

items.q: What is the size of the angle?
items.e: The bottom arm is on 0 on the right, so read the inner scale, which starts at 0 on the right. The other arm crosses it at 155. The small marks go up in 5s, so the mark between 150 and 160 is 155. The outer scale says 25 there, but it starts from the other side. The angle is bigger than a right angle, so 155° makes sense.

items.q: What is the size of the angle?
items.e: The bottom arm is on 0 on the left, so read the outer scale, which starts at 0 on the left. The other arm crosses it at 30. (The inner scale says 150 there.) The angle is smaller than a right angle, so 30° makes sense.

items.q: What is the size of the angle?
items.e: The bottom arm is on 0 on the left, so read the outer scale, which starts at 0 on the left. The other arm crosses it at 120. (The inner scale says 60 there.) The angle is bigger than a right angle, so 120° makes sense.

items.q: What is the size of the angle?
items.e: The bottom arm is on 0 on the left, so read the outer scale, which starts at 0 on the left. The other arm crosses it at 70. (The inner scale says 110 there.) The angle is smaller than a right angle, so 70° makes sense.

items.q: What is the size of the angle?
items.e: The bottom arm is on 0 on the right, so read the inner scale, which starts at 0 on the right. The other arm crosses it at 65. The small marks go up in 5s, so the mark between 60 and 70 is 65. The outer scale says 115 there, but it starts from the other side. The angle is smaller than a right angle, so 65° makes sense.

items.q: The protractor measures the angle between the two arms. What is the reflex angle between the same arms?
items.e: On the inner scale the angle is 75°. The reflex angle goes the other way round. Together they make a revolution: 360° − 75° = 285°. (105° is the reading on the wrong scale.)

items.q: What is the size of the angle?
items.e: The bottom arm is on 0 on the left, so read the outer scale, which starts at 0 on the left. The other arm crosses it at 100. (The inner scale says 80 there.) The angle is bigger than a right angle, so 100° makes sense.

items.q: What is the size of the angle?
items.e: The bottom arm is on 0 on the right, so read the inner scale, which starts at 0 on the right. The other arm crosses it at 110. The outer scale says 70 there, but it starts from the other side. The angle is bigger than a right angle, so 110° makes sense.

items.q: To find a reflex angle, Sienna measures the angle on the other side. It is 130°. What is the reflex angle?
items.e: The two angles go all the way round the vertex, so they make a revolution: 360°. 360° − 130° = 230°. (50° comes from using 180° instead of 360°.)

items.q: What is the size of the angle?
items.e: The bottom arm is on 0 on the left, so read the outer scale, which starts at 0 on the left. The other arm crosses it at 55. The small marks go up in 5s, so the mark between 50 and 60 is 55. (The inner scale says 125 there.) The angle is smaller than a right angle, so 55° makes sense.

items.q: Neither arm is on 0. What is the size of the angle?
items.e: On the inner scale one arm is at 40 and the other is at 150. The angle is the difference: 150° − 40° = 110°.

items.q: One arm of an angle is on 0 of the outer scale. Which scale should you read?
c: the scale with the bigger number
the scale with the smaller number
items.e: Read the scale that starts at 0 on your arm. Here that is the outer scale.

items.q: Mei constructs an angle of 145°, but it looks acute. What went wrong?
items.e: 145° is obtuse, so the angle should look wider than a right angle. On the other scale, 145 is in the same place as 35, so she drew 35°.

items.q: A protractor only goes to 180°. How can you construct a reflex angle of 250°?
c: Draw 70°, then mark the angle outside it
Draw 110°, then mark the angle outside it
items.e: 360° − 250° = 110°. Construct an angle of 110°. The angle round the outside is then 250°. (70° comes from 250° − 180°, but the two angles must make a revolution, 360°.)

items.q: Grace has marked a dot at 35 on the correct scale. What should she do next?
c: Join the dot to the vertex with a ruler
Join the dot to the end of the other arm
Draw a circle through the dot
items.e: The second arm starts at the vertex and goes through the dot. Join them with a ruler, then mark the angle with an arc.

items.q: Matilda is constructing an angle of 65°. What should she do first?
c: Draw a straight arm with a ruler
Draw a dot at 65 on both scales
items.e: First draw one straight arm with a ruler. Then put the centre of the protractor on one end, line the arm up with 0 and mark 65.

items.q: What does a revolution look like when you draw it?
c: One arm, with an arc that goes all the way round back to it
Two arms with an arc round the outside of a gap
Two arms that make a straight line
Two arms that make a right angle
items.e: A revolution is a whole turn, 360°: the arm turns all the way round and ends where it started. Two arms in a straight line make only 180°, a straight angle.
300° is reflex: a revolution (360°) minus 60°. In B the gap is 60° and the arc goes round the outside. A marks only the 60° gap.

items.q: How do you construct a straight angle (180°)?
c: Draw two arms on top of each other
Draw two arms at a right angle
Draw one arm, then carry it on in a straight line past the vertex
Draw an arm that turns all the way round
items.e: A straight angle is half a turn: the two arms point in opposite directions and make one straight line. Two arms at a right angle make only 90°.
135° is a right angle and half a right angle more: D. A is 45° (the wrong scale). C is reflex (225°). B is 160°, nearly a straight angle.
A is a bit less than a right angle: 75°. B is 105° (the wrong scale). C is reflex: its gap is 75°, but the arc marks 285°. D is only 45°.
A straight angle is 180°: the two arms make one straight line. B and D bend a little (170° and 160°). C is reflex (190°): its arc goes past the straight line.

items.q: Noah has drawn one arm. He puts the centre of the protractor on its end, with the arm on 0 of the inner scale. Where should he mark a dot for 65°?
items.e: Use the scale that starts at 0 on your arm: the inner scale. Count up to 65 (the small mark between 60 and 70) and mark a dot there. 65 on the outer scale would give 115°.
D is a bit more than a right angle: 120°. A is 60° (the wrong scale). C is reflex: its gap is 120°, but the arc marks 240°. B is 150°, wider than 120°.

items.q: Leo constructs a 40° angle with arms 10 cm long. Jack constructs a 40° angle with arms 5 cm long. Which angle is bigger?
items.e: The size of an angle is the amount of turn between the arms, not the length of the arms. Both are 40°.

items.q: Which number is in the same place on both scales of a protractor?
items.e: 90 is at the top, halfway round. It is 90 on the inner scale and 90 on the outer scale, so a right angle is the same on both scales.

items.q: Ava wanted to construct an angle of 70°. Her base arm is on 0 of the outer scale. The picture shows what she drew. What angle did she actually draw?
items.e: The base arm is on 0 of the outer scale, so read the outer scale: the second arm is at 110, so the angle is 110°. Ava used 70 on the inner scale by mistake. 180° − 70° = 110°.

items.q: Charlotte wanted to construct an angle of 50°. Her base arm is on 0 of the inner scale. The picture shows what she drew. What angle did she actually draw?
items.e: Read the inner scale, because the base arm is on its 0: the second arm is at 130, so the angle is 130°. Charlotte used 50 on the outer scale by mistake. 180° − 50° = 130°.
210° is reflex: a bit more than a straight angle. C fits. A is 150°, obtuse: its arc goes the short way. D is 330°, nearly a revolution.
B is acute, a bit less than half a right angle: 40°. A is 140°, what you get from the wrong protractor scale. C is a right angle and D is reflex.

items.q: Which drawing shows a right angle?
items.e: A right angle is exactly 90°. C has the small square that shows 90°. A is a little less (80°) and B is a little more (100°).

items.q: To construct a reflex angle of 300°, which angle should you draw first with the protractor?
items.e: The two angles round the vertex make a revolution: 360°. 360° − 300° = 60°. Draw 60°, then mark the big angle round the outside. (120° comes from 300° − 180°.)

items.q: A ceiling fan blade turns 3 revolutions. How many degrees does it turn?
items.e: One revolution is 360°. 3 × 360° = 1080°. (540° comes from using 180° for a revolution.)

items.q: A steering wheel is turned three-quarters of a revolution. How many degrees is that?
items.e: A quarter of a revolution is 360° ÷ 4 = 90°. Three quarters is 3 × 90° = 270°. (135° comes from using 180° for a revolution.)

items.q: What is the name of the marked angle between the hands at 3 o’clock?
items.e: At 3 o’clock the hands are 3 spaces apart: 3 × 30° = 90°. That is a right angle, a quarter turn.

items.q: In skateboarding, a “180” is a jump where the rider turns 180°. How much of a turn is that?
items.e: 180° is half of a revolution (360°): half a turn, a straight angle. The rider ends up facing the other way.

items.q: Harper measures the angle between a playground slide and the ground. She writes 140°, but the angle is clearly acute. What is the angle?
items.e: An acute angle is less than 90°. Harper read the wrong scale: 180° − 140° = 40°.

items.q: Isla opens her laptop so the screen makes an angle of 110° with the keyboard. What is the name of this angle?
items.e: 110° is more than 90° but less than 180°, so it is obtuse.

items.q: What is the size of the marked angle between the hands at 4 o’clock?
items.e: The 12 spaces between the numbers go round a revolution, 360°, so each space is 360° ÷ 12 = 30°. At 4 o’clock the hands are 4 spaces apart: 4 × 30° = 120°.

items.q: Four houses have roof pitches of 15°, 22°, 30° and 40°. Which roof is the steepest?
items.e: The bigger the angle between the roof and the flat ceiling, the steeper the roof. 40° is the largest.

items.q: Aarav faces north on the school oval. He turns until he faces south. How many degrees has he turned?
items.e: North to south is half a turn, whichever way you go: 180°, a straight angle. (360° would bring Aarav back to face north.)

items.q: The minute hand turns clockwise from 12 to 9. How many degrees does it turn?
items.e: 12 to 3, 3 to 6 and 6 to 9 are three quarter turns: 3 × 90° = 270°, a reflex angle. (90° is the short way, from 9 to 12.)

items.q: In one hour the minute hand turns all the way round once. How many degrees does it turn?
items.e: All the way round once is a revolution: 360°. (180° is only half a turn, from 12 to 6.)

items.q: What is the name of the marked angle between the hands at 5 o’clock?
items.e: At 5 o’clock the hands are 5 spaces apart: 5 × 30° = 150°. That is between 90° and 180°, so it is obtuse.

items.q: Ruby’s skateboard ramp makes 20° with the ground. She rebuilds it at 35°. How is the new ramp different?
items.e: A bigger angle with the ground makes a steeper ramp. 35° is bigger than 20°, but both are still acute.

items.q: At 8 o’clock the smaller angle between the hands is 120°. What is the reflex angle between the hands?
items.e: The two angles between the hands make a revolution: 360°. 360° − 120° = 240°. (60° comes from using 180° instead of 360°.)

items.q: The pitch of this roof is the angle between the roof and the flat ceiling. It is 25°. What is the name of this angle?
items.e: 25° is less than 90°, so the roof pitch is an acute angle.

items.q: A skateboarder does a “360”. How much of a turn is that?
items.e: 360° is one whole turn, a revolution: the rider ends up facing the same way again. Half a turn would be a “180”.

items.q: Kai cuts a round birthday cake into 6 equal slices from the centre. What angle does each slice make at the centre?
items.e: The slices go all the way round the centre: a revolution, 360°. 360° ÷ 6 = 60°. (30° comes from using 180° instead of 360°.)

items.q: How many degrees does the minute hand turn in 15 minutes?
items.e: 60 minutes is a revolution (360°). 15 minutes is a quarter of an hour, so a quarter turn: 90°.

items.q: At 6 o’clock the hands of an analog clock point in opposite directions. What angle do they make?
items.e: 6 spaces × 30° = 180°. The hands make one straight line: a straight angle, half a turn. (A revolution would be a whole turn, 360°.)

items.q: This skateboard ramp makes an angle of 20° with the ground. What is the name of this angle?
items.e: 20° is less than 90°, so it is acute. The small square shows the right angle at the back of the ramp.
